title: Finite algebras over a complete Noetherian local ring are products of complete local rings
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring which is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and let $R\to S$ be a ring map making $S$ a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then $S$ is a Noetherian ring with finitely many maximal ideals, and $S$ is isomorphic to a finite product $S_1\times\dots\times S_t$ of Noetherian local rings $(S_j,\mathfrak n_j)$ each of which is $\mathfrak n_j$-adically complete. In particular, if $S$ is a domain, then $S$ is a Noetherian local ring, complete with respect to its maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$, and $\mathfrak n$ is the only prime ideal of $S$ whose inverse image in $R$ is $\mathfrak m$.

proof.text: S is Noetherian by IsNoetherianRing.of_finite R S.

proof.text: Put m = maximalIdeal R, L = R_m, C = the maximal-ideal completion of L. Every denominator outside m is a unit, so IsLocalization.atUnits gives an R-algebra equivalence R ≃ L. The maximal ideal maps to the maximal ideal under this equivalence. Transport adic completeness using IsAdicComplete.congr_ringEquiv; AdicCompletion.ofAlgEquiv then identifies L with C. Composition gives R ≃ₐ[R] C.

source.place: Tags 0325 and 07N9; specialization at the maximal ideal and the domain corollary

proof.text: Apply AdicCompletion.completion_finite_extension at m. It gives finiteness of Q, the type of primes over m, and an S-algebra equivalence C ⊗[R] S ≃ ∏ q : Q, D q, where D q is the completion of S_q at its maximal ideal. Tensor the equivalence R ≃ C of the preceding step with S, and compose with this equivalence restricted to R; this gives S ≃ₐ[R] ∏ q, D q. Integrality makes the contraction of each maximal ideal of S maximal in R, hence equal to m. Sending a maximal ideal to the same ideal regarded as a prime over m is injective, so maximal ideals of S form a finite type.

proof.text: The localizations S_q are Noetherian and local. Their maximal-ideal completions D q are Noetherian by AdicCompletion.isNoetherianRing and local and complete by Mathlib instances from AdicCompletion.LocalRing. Choose Fintype.ofFinite Q and reindex the product through Fintype.equivFin Q using AlgEquiv.piCongrLeft'. This gives exactly the required Fin t product, including the empty product when S is the zero ring.

source.place: Tags 0325 and 07N9; specialization at the maximal ideal and the domain corollary

proof.text: Suppose S is a domain. If Q were empty, the product would be subsingleton and the equivalence would give 1 = 0 in S. If i and j in Q were distinct, define x(q) = 1 when q = i and 0 otherwise, and y(q) = 0 when q = i and 1 otherwise. Then xy = 0, but x(i) = 1 and y(j) = 1 in nontrivial local factors. Applying the inverse equivalence contradicts the absence of zero divisors in S. Thus Q is nonempty and subsingleton, giving Unique Q. RingEquiv.piUnique composed with the product equivalence identifies S with the one factor.

proof.text: Transport localness using RingEquiv.isLocalRing and completeness using IsAdicComplete.congr_ringEquiv and IsLocalRing.map_ringEquiv_maximalIdeal. The maximal ideal contracts to m by integrality. If a prime M contracts to m, Ideal.isMaximal_of_isIntegral_of_isMaximal_comap makes M maximal, and IsLocalRing.eq_maximalIdeal identifies it with the maximal ideal of S.
